extDescription.message: Progressively translates Discord Web chat messages and forum post titles

options_providerGemini.message: Gemini (API key required, better with gaming slang)

options_deeplKeyHelpPrefix.message: You can get a free key from the

options_deeplKeyHelpSuffix.message: (free keys end with ":fx"). If DeepL hits its limit, it automatically falls back to Gemini (if configured), then Google Translate.

options_deeplUsageEmptyKey.message: Enter an API key to check usage.

options_deeplUsageError.message: Couldn't fetch usage (please check your API key).

options_geminiKeyHelpPrefix.message: You can get a free key (no credit card required) from

options_geminiKeyHelpBold.message: This is separate from the paid Gemini App plans (Gemini Pro, etc.)

options_geminiKeyHelpMiddle2.message: , and login credentials aren't shared, so you must issue and enter an API key here. It tends to handle gaming terms and slang more naturally than machine translation, but tone can vary a bit between messages and it's a little slower. Safety filters are relaxed so dark-fantasy game vocabulary (e.g. "Flayed") doesn't get blocked. The free tier is capped at 15 requests/minute, so if a lot of messages get auto-translated at once, the extra ones are automatically routed to DeepL/Google Translate before hitting that limit. On failure it automatically falls back to DeepL (if configured), then Google Translate.

options_geminiToneAuto.message: Let it vary naturally with each message

options_geminiCustomPromptHelp.message: A plain request like "do X" is sometimes too weak. Adding a [MOST IMPORTANT RULE] plus 1-2 conversion examples works much better (e.g. "[MOST IMPORTANT RULE] Always end sentences with 'nya'. [Example] This is great -> This is great, nya"). Requests for extreme content changes may be ignored.

options_languageHelp.message: Fixing the source language means translate buttons only appear on messages in that language (e.g. fixing it to Japanese means English messages in the same thread won't get a button). Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian, and Thai are detected by script; other languages (EN/FR/DE/ES/PT/IT/VI/ID) use a simple Latin-script heuristic. Setting the target to "Auto (browser language)" translates according to your browser's display language. This language setting also applies to Gemini.

options_skipShortLabel.message: Don't show for very short messages

options_providerPlamo.message: Local (PLaMo 3 Translate, runs on your PC)

options_plamoErrBadUrl.message: Enter the URL as http://localhost:PORT or http://127.0.0.1:PORT.

options_plamoErrUnreachable.message: Can't reach the server. Check that it's running and the port is correct.

options_plamoErrNoModel.message: Connected, but no PLaMo model is loaded on the server.

options_plamoErrOllamaOrigin.message: Ollama refused the connection. Set the environment variable OLLAMA_ORIGINS to chrome-extension://* and restart Ollama.

options_plamoHelp.message: PLaMo 3 Translate must be running on your PC (the 2B Q4_K_M build is recommended). Translation stays on your PC and nothing is sent outside. Only servers on your own PC (localhost) are allowed. If translation fails, it falls back to DeepL or Gemini when their API keys are set, then to Google Translate. Portuguese isn't supported, so it's translated by another engine.

popup_extensionEnabledHelpShort.message: When off, nothing runs, including the blue bars

popup_autoTranslateHelpShort.message: Auto-translation starts from your first click

popup_openOptionsHelpShort.message: Set the engine, languages, and display rules.

popup_captchaHelpShort.message: Opens the "I'm not a robot" check page in a new tab.
